text: I'm queer and proud, and honestly this lesson on the Stonewall riots made me tear up. Took us decades to wear that word like a crown instead of a wound.
note: self-identifying pride, reclaiming own group's term

text: As a Black woman in tech I love how my girls and I call each other queens in our study group chat. Reclaiming our worth one calc problem at a time lol.
Crip and unbothered. The disability rights chapter finally framed us as a community, not a tragedy. We use that word with each other on purpose, it's ours now.
note: disabled person reclaiming in-group term, pride

text: Fat acceptance class checking in. Yep, I said fat, not 'plus size' or whatever soft word makes thin people comfortable. It's a neutral descriptor and I'm reclaiming it.
note: reclaiming descriptor about own body, no attack

text: Us nerds finally inherited the earth, didn't we? Whole module is basically my high-school bullies' worst nightmare. Wear the label proudly, fellow geeks.
Bi disaster here and the bisexuality history section was *chef's kiss*. We joke about being a disaster, it's our own term of endearment, don't @ me about it.
My deaf friends and I sign 'Deaf gain' instead of hearing loss now. This course gets it. We're not broken hearing people, we're whole Deaf people with our own culture.
note: Deaf community pride, reframing own identity

text: Spinster. There, I said it about myself and I mean it as a compliment. The women's history lecture reminded me unmarried women built half the libraries in this country.
note: reclaiming gendered slur about herself, pride

text: Trailer trash and damn proud of where I grew up. The Appalachia poverty chapter actually let us speak for ourselves for once instead of gawking at us.
note: reclaiming class slur about own background

text: Old hag reporting for duty in the gerontology unit. My granddaughters and I call each other that all the time. At 78 I've earned every grey hair and every cackle.
note: elder reclaiming ageist term, family banter

text: Recovering addict, eight years clean. In meetings we call ourselves junkies sometimes, takes the shame out of it. This addiction-science module never once treated us like garbage, and that meant everything.
note: in-recovery person reclaiming term, no dehumanisation
